why: B, C and D are true statements a careless reader could take as false (B by looking only at the 5s, where current customers lead 19% to 14%; C because cooking time's 90% sits right next to value for money's 93%; D by misreading the low ratings), and the likely slip of comparing percentages instead of counts makes A look true, so it does not land on the answer.

The options form a tight grid at a steady ratio, each about 10% from the next (2,094 / 2,309 / 2,537 / 2,816), so a rough estimate or an arithmetic slip lands on a neighbour (applying the May–June 15% margin to July revenue gives about 2,870, near 2,816), and no common slip lands on 2,537.

The options are a tight even grid with steps of 0.2 (about 8% of the answer), and rounding B's share to a fifth gives 2.66, which lands on £2.6m; slips that move the working (dropping the fixed cost gives 1.66, using the cumulative 29% gives 3.86) land well away from £2.4m.

The options are a tight even grid with steps of 1.5 points (16% of the answer), and taking margin on costs instead of revenue gives 14.8% − 3.6% = 11.2, which lands on 10.9; the near-answer 9.1 from dividing the profit gap by revenue is the estimate the shortcut uses, not a slip in the working.

The options are every year shown, and the slips that still land on 2009 (comparing absolute online profits while ignoring the sales base, or comparing growth) are the ones sourceHas names, so they match the source.

A reads Region 2's largest share, or its close 23% point, as the top margin, while B and C are over-readings that treat similar or lowest market shares as equal profit or lowest sales without market sizes; the misreads that still give twice (half a gridline off, or a neighbouring point) are the ones sourceHas names.
The options are every country on offer, and the slips that still make B highest (multiplying by the cost column or by price instead of weight) are the ones sourceHas names, so they match the source.
$34.4bn reads the second bar's height (40% × 86), $69.5bn applies the right 15% to worldwide spending of $463bn, and $185.2bn makes both slips (40% × 463).
$240,000 less reverses the sign, $450,000 more ignores the tier and prices all 450,000 kg at $5, and $450,000 less combines the ignored tier with a reversed sign.

C multiplies by 152 instead of dividing, B makes the same slip and also brings in the irrelevant hourly rate p, and D turns C upside down (multiplies by 152 and divides the wrong way round); each takes one or two slips.
